extracted.intended_audience: PTAB judges and PTAB Executive Management (PTAB staff involved in decision review processes)
extracted.subtask_description: Standard Operating Procedure for optional internal circulation and review of PTAB decisions prior to issuance and for post-issuance review to identify decisions warranting Director review or policy clarification. It defines reviewer pools, membership, review processes, duties, and conflict-of-interest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional Circulation to Circulation Judge Pool (CJP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any panel member, at his or her sole discretion, may choose to circulate a draft decision to a designated pool of non-management peer judges (the “Circulation Judge Pool” or “CJP”) prior to issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When CJP review is requested, the decision typically is reviewed by two CJP members (“reviewers”). Each reviewer may edit the draft by providing comments and/or suggested revisions. Reviewers may discuss comments with the broader CJP at regular committee meetings; after consensus on discussed items, a redlined draft is sent to the panel for consideration. The CJP may elect a single brief review or decline review if workload or impending deadlines prevent fuller review. The CJP may provide information regarding potential conflicts or inconsistencies with relevant authority, potential inconsistencies with other PTAB decisions, and suggestions for improved readability and stylistic consistency. The CJP’s comments are optional suggestions; the panel has final authority on whether and how to incorporate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJP membership criteria and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: CJP membership is open to any non-management PTAB judge and includes at least six members who collectively have technical/scientific backgrounds and legal experience representative of the PTAB judges as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical CJP member qualities: thinks critically about nuances in the law, has an attention to detail, and keeps up-to-date on applicable written guidance and policy, Board decisions including precedential cases, and Federal Circuit and Supreme Court case law regarding patentability issues and PTAB practice. Members typically serve one-year staggered terms with overlap for orientation. PTAB Executive Management solicits volunteers and selects members in consultation with supervisors to achieve balanced representation and sufficient workload capacity. Each CJP member receives production credit for CJP-related work.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJP interface with PTAB Executive Management
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJP may have periodic meetings with PTAB Executive Management to discuss issued decisions that address notable issues, potentially conflict with relevant authority or other PTAB decisions, and general areas for potential policy clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB Executive Management may discuss issues or issued decisions flagged by the CJP with the Director for purposes such as (i) considering whether to issue new or updated policies or guidance (via regulation, precedential/informative decisions, or Director guidance memoranda), and (ii) considering sua sponte Director review of a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional Pre-Issuance Consultation with PTAB Management Pre-Issuance Optional Review team
rubrics_metrics.description: Any panel member, at his or her sole discretion, may optionally request input from a PTAB Management Pre-Issuance Optional Review team regarding a decision prior to issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTAB Management Pre-Issuance Optional Review team is designated by PTAB Executive Management and may include Vice Chief Judges, Senior Lead Judges, Lead Judges, and those acting in such positions. Their input may include information regarding potential conflicts or inconsistencies with relevant authority or other PTAB decisions. They may consult senior management in another USPTO business unit for input and may share that input with the panel if solicited. The panel’s adoption of any suggestions is optional. Unless requested by a panel member (or they are on the panel), the Pre-Issuance team does not provide input on pre-issuance decisions, and they do not provide input to the CJP regarding a CJP review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel final authority and responsibility for content of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB panel has final authority and responsibility for the content of a decision, and determines whether and in what manner, if at all, to incorporate any feedback received from the CJP or the PTAB Management Pre-Issuance Optional Review team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to incorporate feedback from the CJP or PTAB Management Pre-Issuance Optional Review team has no effect in and of itself on a PTAB judge’s performance review. Nevertheless, judges are required by their Performance Appraisal Plan to apply pertinent statutes, regulations, binding case law, and written guidance issued by the Director or the Director’s delegate; failure to follow those binding authorities could impact performance review regardless of whether feedback was sought or received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to apply pertinent statutes, regulations, and binding guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB judges are required by their Performance Appraisal Plan (PAP) to apply pertinent statutes, regulations, binding case law, and written guidance issued by the Director or the Director’s delegate that is applicable to PTAB proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written agency or Board policy or guidance that is binding on judges is made public. Judges’ noncompliance with these binding authorities may affect performance evaluations even where optional pre-issuance review was sought or provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unwritten binding agency/Board policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no unwritten agency or Board policy or guidance applicable to PTAB proceedings that judges are required to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any written agency or Board policy or guidance that is binding on judges is made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurring and dissenting opinions permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: When judges on a panel have additional or dissenting views, they may express those views in concurring or dissenting opinions as they deem appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such views are an important part of the judicial process and may be impactful to the Director in deciding whether to review a decision post-issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Director pre-issuance involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director, Deputy Director, Commissioner for Patents, and Commissioner for Trademarks will not be involved pre-issuance, directly or indirectly, in directing or otherwise influencing any panel decisions unless they are a panel member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to SOP 1, the Director has delegated authority to assign judges to panels to the Chief Judge and delegates. The Director will not be involved in directing or influencing paneling or repaneling prior to issuance of the panel decision. When reviewing or rehearing an issued panel decision, the Director may direct repaneling consistent with PTAB paneling guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Issuance Review team responsibilities and flagging criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A PTAB Post-Issuance Review team reviews issued PTAB decisions and flags certain decisions for consideration for Director-initiated (sua sponte) review or policy clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Post-Issuance Review team may identify decisions that, for example, address an issue of first impression, appear inconsistent with relevant authority, or involve an area where policy clarification may be needed. After identifying a decision, the team determines whether to flag it for PTAB Executive Management, which then decides whether to flag it to the Director for further attention such as sua sponte Director review or other review/policy clarification mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest notification and recusal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a member of the CJP, the PTAB Management Pre-Issuance Optional Review Team, or the PTAB Post-Issuance Review team has a conflict of interest, they shall notify the other members of their respective team and will recuse themselves from any discussion or analysis of that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining whether a conflict exists, the USPTO follows guidance set forth in the Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch at 5 CFR Part 2635 and will consult with the Department of Commerce Ethics Law and Programs Office as necessary. Conflicts may include involvement in the examination or prosecution of the underlying patent or a related patent at issue. As policy, members of those teams will also follow conflicts guidance in SOP 1 and will recuse from any discussion or analysis involving cases or related cases on which they are paneled.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJP workload and timing accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a decision is submitted close to an impending deadline when the CJP workload is too heavy to accommodate the deadline, the CJP may elect to have one CJP member conduct a brief review or may decline to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to balance timely issuance of decisions with availability of CJP resources; panels remain responsible for final content even when CJP declines or provides limited review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limits on Pre-Issuance Management input
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB Management Pre-Issuance Optional Review team does not provide feedback on decisions prior to issuance unless they are a member of the panel or a panel member requests such feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if a CJP review is requested, the PTAB Management Pre-Issuance Optional Review team does not provide any input to the CJP regarding that review. The panel member may indicate if they sought input from another USPTO business unit when requesting PTAB Management input.
